drop-p087291-jincheng-cbm.drop_reason: No completion report and no appraisal document exist for this operation: the Bank's document list for P087291 holds eight items. The only outcome documents are three Implementation Status and Results Reports, of 25 February 2012, 4 June 2012 and 17 May 2013, and all three were read in full. They record that the 120 MW coal-mine methane power plant was commissioned in October 2008, that the agreed Environmental Management Plan, Resettlement Action Plan and Safety Management Plan 'have been followed during the operation of the project', and that one safety problem - gas storage tanks too close to an existing railway line - was fixed with a dividing wall agreed between Zhengzhou Railway Bureau and the project company. No person, household or dwelling is counted in any of the three. The 23 households and 85 persons, the 79.8 mu and the three village names in the resettlement action plan of 25 April 2004 are all in the future tense ('will be', 'is planned'), and no document records the acquisition happening. A title search for a completion report returned nothing beyond those eight items. The money was a Prototype Carbon Fund purchase of emission reductions, not a loan for the works.

drop-p100968-shanxi-cbm.drop_reason: Annex 10 of the completion report of 18 June 2018 was read end to end, all nine paragraphs. It is an outcome account: 112 mu acquired for the LNG plant site from Dongshan and Jinfeng villages, 13 households compensated for 12.8 mu of contracted land and given replacement farmland, 132 mu occupied temporarily with CNY 0.75 million paid, 896 mu for the gas wells with all compensation paid, and eight external resettlement monitoring reports finding the process and outcome satisfactory for the affected people. Paragraph 8 records the one loose end: a 14 mu gas storage site not formally acquired as of March 2018, with civil works going ahead under a temporary occupation arrangement agreed with the local government and full compensation promised once the land-use readjustment in Qinshui County is approved. The supplement resettlement plan of November 2012 states that the gas storage stations involve only unused land, so no crop, dwelling or trading place sits on the 14 mu, and no person or household is counted against it. The Evaluation Group's review of 14 December 2018 omits paragraph 8 altogether and says all compensation was paid; that disagreement is reported below. No relocation and no unpaid loss to an identifiable person appears in either document.

drop-p121263-gef-eco-transport.drop_reason: Re-read the completion report of 26 December 2016. Paragraph 16 states 'The Grant financed technical assistance, advisory and capacity building services'; paragraph 630 of the component account states that the two terminals 'was financed 100% by counterpart fund of US$ 27.27 million' from the Hunan Department of Transport. Paragraph 28, the social safeguards paragraph, says a resettlement action plan 'was prepared for Western Changsha Hub for the acquisition of 18 mu of rural land and relocation of 65 urban and 54 rural households', and that post-project interviews confirmed compensation rates, procedures and consultation were as promised, that no complaints were received, and that external monitoring showed incomes rose afterwards through lease income from compensation apartments. The verb in the one sentence carrying a household figure attaches to what the plan was prepared for, not to a recorded outcome, and the figure does not match the project's own plan: the January 2011 resettlement action plan RP1093 counts 64 households and 240 persons losing residential houses, 8 on collective land and 56 on state-owned land, plus 46 households living in transitional sheds built when they were moved for an earlier project. For the Lituo hub, built on an existing high-speed rail station site, a due diligence review was prepared instead of a plan. No outcome document counts anyone relocated, and the works where people were moved were paid for by the borrower, not by grant TF099421.

drop-p129563-anhui-yellow-mountain.drop_reason: Read paragraphs 71 to 73 of the completion report of 21 December 2020 with their footnotes, and the Evaluation Group's review of 8 June 2021. The report's outcome sentence: 'although the project supported a large number of facility improvements, only 22 ha of farmland were acquired at closing and there was no physical relocation of affected persons. The 1,914 affected persons were compensated as required.' Footnote 26 explains the mechanism - under the 2004 Chinese land law village committees terminate farmers' land contracts where the land goes to village public interests and farmers are compensated - and footnote 27 records one land-exchange scheme, in Sanhe Village of Huangshan District. The review adds two figures the report does not carry: 546 families with 1,914 people affected by the 22 hectares, and 1.26 hectares (18.95 mu) used temporarily during construction, 'involved 39 households (130 people) that caused seasonal economic losses', with the land later returned to the farmers. The review attributes those to an end-of-project social survey, not to a staff statement. Nobody was relocated; land was taken, compensation was paid, the temporarily taken land went back, and the resettlement agencies at city, district, county and township level recorded no complaints. That is land area plus a count of affected people, which is a drop on this map. The 39 households with seasonal losses are recorded here so the owner can reverse this if a compensated seasonal crop loss is judged a harm.

drop-p099224-liaoning-third-medium-citie.drop_reason: Re-read paragraphs 60 to 63 of the completion report of 20 December 2016. They record that resettlement action plans were prepared and approved at appraisal for the Yingkou Dashiqiao, Benxi Nanfen and Huludao subprojects; that none of the four subprojects added during implementation involved land acquisition because they built pipelines and substations; that for the Chaoyang subproject a due diligence review confirmed the associated combined heat and power site had completed its land acquisition and resettlement before joining the project; and that according to the project office's monitoring reports 'all affected people were compensated for land acquisition and rehabilitation measures in accordance with the RAPs'. There is no demolition figure, no relocation figure and no count of people anywhere in the section. On the small coal boilers the report records redeployment of affected boiler workers into heat supply companies with skill training, reported to the Bank every six months, and gives no count of job losses. The 956 persons from 308 households and the 562 persons in 179 households are appraisal and plan figures; the later plans of 2010, 2012, 2013 and 2014 carry no outcome figures.

drop-p111325-dashiqiao-heating.drop_reason: No completion report exists for this number and none was found by title search; the Bank's list holds 15 items, the latest an implementation status report of 19 December 2014, which was read. It states 'This is a subproject under Liaoning Third Medium Cities Infrastructure Project (P099224)'. The two documents filed as this project's resettlement plans are both volumes of RP590, the parent project's resettlement policy framework. The operation itself was a purchase of emission reductions, with board approval given as the emission reductions purchase agreement of 31 December 2009. The parent project's completion report of 20 December 2016, read for P099224 above, carries no count of anyone relocated at Dashiqiao or anywhere else.

drop-p093882-shandong-fgd.drop_reason: Read the completion report of 21 December 2012 in full on this point. Paragraphs 27 and 28 record that three of the four power plants named at appraisal - Laiwu, Huangtai and Yantai - were dropped before the loan became effective because other financing was found, and that of the four only the Lubei plant was partly implemented, with one contract of US$14,962,500, after which the Bank team found fraudulent practices, the funds were reimbursed in June 2011 and the loan amount was cancelled. The Lubei flue-gas unit sat inside an existing power plant and needed no land. Section 2.4 on safeguards discusses only the environmental assessment and a late change from a calcium-based to a magnesium-based desulfurisation technology; paragraph 46 of the same report says of poverty impacts, gender aspects and social development: 'Not applicable.' The Evaluation Group's review of 9 June 2015 notes that the report has no social safeguards section at all. Fraud that killed a subproject is not harm to identifiable people, and no land acquisition or relocation happened anywhere under this loan.

drop-p112626-liuzhou-environment-ii.drop_reason: Two outcome documents were read. The updated resettlement plan of October 2015 is headed 'Updated impact after completing land acquistion' and gives planned against actual in one table: 117.24 mu of rural collective land permanently acquired against 107.9 mu planned, affecting 57 households with 255 persons in Jila village, Yangjiaoshan town, Yufeng district and Baisha village, Jingxiu sub-district, Liubei district; and 8,134.9 square metres of structures demolished against 2,503.9 planned, affecting 23 households with 118 persons. What was demolished was not housing. At Longquanshan it was 'rural field attendance houses (non-residential)' in Jila village, 18 households and 87 persons, 'compensated for'. At Baisha the 5,631.01 square metres were the premises of five entities on an extra 19.13 mu taken for urban landscaping and road construction - Liuzhou Jinhui Material Recycling Co., Ltd., Huangsheng Pig-raising Equipment Co., Ltd., an equipment lease warehouse, the Longyue Baisha car park, and prefabricated construction houses used as the temporary quarters of the construction team of the Green Cloud residential community - with 31 persons in 5 households. The completion report of 21 February 2019 counts nobody relocated and states at paragraph 79 that 'Independent reviews showed that livelihoods of affected persons have fully recovered or became better off after the completion of land acquisition and resettlement', with delays in land acquisition caused by legacy issues and the city's urbanisation master plans; the borrower's own section adds that part of the land acquisition and relocation could not be done as originally planned. Land taken with compensation paid, non-residential structures demolished, and livelihoods reported recovered. The five Baisha premises are recorded again here so the owner can reverse this if business premises demolished are judged trading places taken.

vietnam-redp-small-hydro-land.drop_reason: Re-read the completion report of 14 December 2018. Paragraph 44 and paragraph 82 both carry the figures. Paragraph 82: 'the project implementation did not involve significant resettlement and no adverse socioeconomic impacts have been recorded. In total, the project required reallocation of less than 50 households and approximately 2,500 households were affected in terms of loss of agricultural/tree crop land and sources of income. The land acquisition, compensation, livelihood restoration, and ethnic minority development were implemented complying with the RPs and EMDPs.' Paragraph 44 gives the same two figures as 'less than 50' and 'more than 2,000'. 'Less than 50' is a ceiling, not a count, and no plant, province or community is named for any of it; the paragraph names the only problems as minor, 'some minor issues such as slightly late compensations', addressed on time, and a grievance mechanism at village, commune and district level. Footnote 31 records that the developers paid all resettlement costs. The sited material - including the Ha Tay plan for Chu Pah district, Gia Lai province, with 211 square metres of residential land of 7 households and 4 of them relocating in place - is in the subproject resettlement plans, which are plans. No outcome document for Ha Tay or any other plant was found.

taunsa-barrage-basti-shaikhan-relocation.drop_reason: Duplicate, confirmed again by place and years rather than by number. The map already carries taunsa-barrage-relocation at Taunsa Barrage, Indus River, Punjab, Pakistan, 2005 to 2009, resting on the same US$123 million loan approved 15 March 2005, the same completion report and the same Evaluation Group review, and it already holds the two villages moved in June 2005 at the contractor's request, the breach of OP 4.12, the 160 families and about 900 people, the canal closures, the 38 people indicted and Descon's protest. That case carries no P-number, which is why the dedupe script still reports P088994 as absent. Not re-opened; the P-number should be added to the existing case's lender role.

Ghana Urban Transport Project.drop_reason: Re-read, and the drop reason changes. The completion report of 26 January 2017 says at paragraph 39 that 'The process of land acquisition for the terminal was prolonged due to disputes among community leaders but the shifting of the route from the BRT corridor to the QBS corridor made these anticipated land acquisitions unnecessary', and the Evaluation Group's review of 9 June 2017 says 'No land acquisition was required as BRT component was dropped'. The borrower's own comments, in the same completion report, contradict both: 'Executive Instruments for compulsory acquisition of the depot and terminal were issued. DUR has formally paid compensation for the depot.' So land was compulsorily acquired, and the works went ahead - the report's results annex records 27 bus stops, terminals at Achimota and Amasaman and one depot built. What no document gives is any person, household, trader or sum: the borrower names no owner and no amount, says compensation for the depot was paid, and says nothing either way about the terminal. The ten implementation status reports from 2010 to 2015 were read for land acquisition and carry nothing beyond one line in December 2012 that the plans were completed. The 119 traders in the abbreviated resettlement plan of July 2014 are described there as 'likely to lose their specific sites upon the implementation' - a plan. One search outside the Bank found shops demolished at Neoplan station and Kwame Nkrumah Circle in October 2014 by the Department of Urban Roads, the same agency, but for the three-tier Circle interchange, which this credit did not finance. The Evaluation Group also criticises the report for giving no supporting information on safeguards for a category A project, so this remains the weakest of the drops.

ID-Domestic Gas Market Development Proje.drop_reason: Re-read paragraphs 66 to 72 of the completion report of 30 April 2014 in full. Paragraph 70: 'Gas distribution pipelines did not require any land acquisition because they were installed roadside rights of way', with permission from the Ministry of Public Works and local governments, and pipe-laying in the market area done outside business hours and mainly at night 'in order to greatly minimize any potential negative economic impacts on local traders'. Paragraph 69: land was acquired for five meter regulation stations in four locations. Paragraph 68: the process 'used a normal transaction approach with market price as a basis for land value, similar to a willing-seller, willing-buyer transaction'. Paragraph 71(iii): 'During supervision, there were no complaints regarding the level of compensation paid for land acquired for the Bojeonegara-Serpong transmission pipeline' - and that pipeline was financed by PGN and JBIC, not by loan 4810-ID, the Bank monitoring it only because of the linkage. The planned Serpong off-take station was replaced by two stations at Bitung because suitable land could not be found, so it was never built. No person, household or trader is counted as losing anything.

Brasilia Environmentally Sustainable Pro.drop_reason: Duplicate, confirmed by number. The dedupe script reports P089440 as already on the map as brasilia-vila-estrutural-resettlement, Vila Estrutural and Monjolo, Federal District, Brazil, 2008 to 2012, and that case already carries the P-number, the US$57.64 million loan, the 903 figure, the 7 May 2010 disbursement suspension with its partial and full lifting, the 34 households put into temporary housing, the families placed in tents and wooden shacks, the four moved against their will and the 242 households still waiting in May 2012. Not re-opened.

The dedupe script reports P115767 as already on the map as bharatpur-bardaghat-line-dumkibas, Dumkibas, Binayi Triveni Rural Municipality Ward No. 2, Nawalpur, Nepal, 2011 to 2024, which rests on the Inspection Panel's report and names the credit, the additional financing and the 74 km Bharatpur-Bardaghat line. Peru Safe and Sustainable Transport Proj.drop_reason: Re-read the last outcome document there is: the archived Implementation Status and Results Report, sequence 3, of 15 November 2010. It gives loan IBRD-78320 as 'Not Effective', US$150.00 million original, US$150.00 million revised, US$0.00 cancelled, US$0.00 disbursed, US$150.00 million undisbursed. Approval was 14 January 2010 and the closing date 22 March 2011. No completion report exists under this number and a title search found none. The compensation and involuntary resettlement plans for Villa Rica, Cochabamba-Chota and Llama-Cochabamba are appraisal-stage plans with no outcome document behind them. Nothing was disbursed, so no harm can overlap the lender's involvement.

20 MW Palinpinon II Geothermal Optimizat.drop_reason: Re-read the Note on Cancelled Operation of 29 June 2012, which is the only outcome document. It states that 'no CER was realized to date as the Power Plant and FCRS have not been constructed' and that the Energy Development Corporation 'had not undertaken any monitoring as there were no physical activities in the project site'. The emission reduction purchase agreement was defaulted on 30 April 2010 and terminated. The note calls the resettlement at the site 'a legacy issue of the existing Palinpinon I and II projects' and states that 'The families to be resettled were not displaced by Nasulo or by Palinpinon I and II but they will be resettled for their own long term safety and development in a site being developed nearby.' Of 194 households identified and 153 named in a draft plan, 29 had been resettled by 17 June 2011, 13 to the company's resettlement village and 16 to sites of their own choosing. Nothing was built, nothing was paid out under the agreement, and the note attributes the moves to safety at pre-existing works.

Integrated Municipal Project - Betim Mun.drop_reason: The closest call of the nineteen, and the drop stands. Both outcome documents were read end to end on this point. The completion report of 3 June 2010 records that 887 families were resettled, 330 into the newly built Conjunto Celso Pedrosa and 557 on cash compensation, and that the resettlement was needed 'In order to execute drainage works, interceptors, and the rehabilitation of rivers banks and green areas'. Its annex then says: 'When compensations would be too small in value (below R$ 10,000) to allow families to purchase a new house, these were resettled in the Conjunto Celso Pedrosa' - the same sentence states the remedy, a house, so the report does not record anyone left with compensation below the price of a house. The highest compensations reached R$20,000, at R$1.80 to the dollar. The annex also says the project's social team 'had to work hard in order to convince these families to accept a new house in the Conjunto rather than financial compensation', with no count of families and no recorded compulsion; that families who took compensation 'were monitored for a short time and most of them moved to other cities'; that no new survey of the resettled families was carried out by the municipality; that an area in the estate set aside for social facilities such as a school 'has not been constructed so far'; and that there is 'an alleged high rate of sale of housing units by resettled families'. The Evaluation Group's Project Performance Assessment Report of 14 March 2011, the only field-based document, visited Betim in January 2010 and found at 4.11 that the 887 families 'were resettled peacefully from flood-prone canal and river banks', that affected families contacted during the field visits confirmed the arrangements, and that several beneficiaries said they had opportunities to question the compensation and housing offered 'but most did not, finding the conditions offered to be adequate'; at 4.12 five families in Celso Pedrosa said their present houses 'were far superior to their previous dwellings'. Much of 4.11 is prefaced 'As described to IEG by Betim municipality officials'. A relocation out of flood-prone banks, with no loss recorded on top of the move that carries a count, is the shape BRIEF20's Bogota rule excludes.

Irrigation & Watershed Management Projec.drop_reason: Re-read the completion report of 24 June 2015. The only resettlement it records is at paragraph 37, that 'the Government contributed a substantial budget towards the implementation of the Ankaibe weir and feeder canal resettlement action plan', with safeguards rated Satisfactory at project end; the Ankaibe weir and feeder canal were not in the original design and were added later. No count of houses, people or households appears anywhere in the report. The Ankaibe resettlement plan of June 2013, filed under the parent number P074086, inventories the losses as land in the right of way, standing crops, and economic activity consisting only of land rental ('Les activites economiques existantes sont seulement la location de terrains'), affecting 141 households who own or farm plots plus three legal entities, and puts construction compensation for buildings and fences at 6,508,000 Ariary against 271,960,044 for crops and 148,885,506 for land. No dwelling lost, no relocation, no outcome figure.

Fifth Power System Development Project.drop_reason: Re-read the completion report of 13 August 2020, including the footnote under the results table. The 'Percent of PAPs rehabilitated' indicator is reported at 100 per cent of target, and footnote b under it reads: 'No involuntary land acquisition was involved, and land purchased was only on the willing buyer, willing seller basis.' Paragraph 63 records about 1,000 acres for 13 substations and 20 transmission lines of about 7,308 circuit-km, direct purchases on that basis at Aurangabad and Kolhapur, an annuity arrangement elsewhere, and that 'Designing has been done such as to avoid tribal and other densely populated habitations'; impact assessments are reported as finding that project-affected persons and nearby communities benefited relative to before. The project's two published rehabilitation action plans count 51 project-affected families at the Solapur 765 kV substation and 155 at Indore, both agricultural land plans whose only mentions of houses are generic entitlement-matrix lines. Land area plus a count of affected people, with no dwelling lost and no unpaid or short compensation recorded.
